Steam Family Sharing lets anyone in your family play the games you bought, but only as many copies at once as you bought. If my wife owns a copy of game A and I start playing it on my account (which doesn't own a copy of game A), she can play game B on her account just fine. But if she loads up game A she's told "someone else from your Steam family is currently playing that game". So it depends on what you mean by "simultaneous play". Game A and game B played at once, yes. Game A played by two people at once when you own one copy, no. For the record, I'm 100% fine with that.

> or do founders become metaphorical indentured servants? VCs invest in the company. They put money into the company and get equity in the company in return. It’s not a loan to the founders. So don’t worry, they’re not indentured servants and everyone, including the VCs, knew this was a possible outcome. In VC it’s actually the most likely outcome because most companies don’t become big successes or even become valuable stable businesses. What happens next: The remaining assets and liabilities will be settled up. Any remaining cash goes to the owners (equity), generally with some preference to paying back most recent investors first up (preference). If the founders performed well and the investors believed they were doing good work that didn’t pan out due to market conditions or bad luck, they may be interested in investing with those founders again later. Or they may be sour and not want to talk to them. I’ve seen more of the former than the latter. Most VCs try to avoid getting bad reputations so they’ll make an effort to stay on good terms with founders.
